Corrected keys carry new names, so the eight other locales fall back to the corrected English per key instead of repeating the old wording. Hosting: "no production processing outside the EU" -> servers, DB and storage are in the EU; Resend (email) and xAI (AI prefill, only when an organization switches data sharing on, default off) are US services under SCCs. 2. Encryption at rest: "PostgreSQL data on Hetzner infrastructure" implied DB encryption -> S3 objects are AES256 (incl. archived invoices); the application does not encrypt PostgreSQL. 3. Login rate limit: per application instance -> per email address and app instance, in memory, every attempt counts; sessions end after eight hours. 4. Roles: Admin, Reviewer, Member -> Admin, Reviewer, Legal Reviewer, Member. 5. Tenant separation "at the database layer" -> in the application, filtered on the session's company I

sources.observed_relation: Hi Amir, I wrote UCCI (arXiv:2605.18796), which `mini_ork/dispatch/calibration.py` ports. The paper's reference implementation is now public: https://github.com/varunkotte6/ucci (`pip install ucci-router`). Since `calibration.py` keeps PAV dependency-free, the part most likely to be useful here is the golden vectors in `tests/golden/calibration.json`. They are generated from the reference code (and matched bit for bit by an independent Rust port), and the equal-weight PAV cases, including ties, map directly onto `pav(values)`. A small test that runs them would pin the port's behaviour as the module evolves. Happy to open a PR adding that test if it would help. Varun Kotte
sources.title: UCCI reference implementation and golden test vectors for dispatch/calibration.py
